To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) a high plane of nutrition during the first 10 days post-ovulation in sheep compromises pregnancy establishment; (ii) a high plane during early pregnancy does not alter the secretion of luteotrophic proteins by the conceptus; and (iii) a high plane post-ovulation results in a reduction in peripheral concentrations of progesterone during early pregnancy.

1) overfeeding during the first week after ovulation compromises embryo survival, but not growth, in vivo, and 2) overfeeding does not alter the luteotrophic capacity of conceptuses in vitro, despite a reduction in circulating progesterone.
overfeeding during early pregnancy does not affect the ability of the endometrium to support conceptus development in vivo or to secrete luteotrophic proteins in vitro.
